text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis is on a visit to Estonia. He addressed parliament in a speech in favour of closer cooperation between the Baltic states.
- The government plans to open six more embassies in the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, Greece and Ireland.
- The border guard bought a patrol boat from Sweden for one million kroons. The boat will patrol the area around the island of Ruhnu in seas to the south west of Estonia.
- Students accuse the government of cheating them about the promised increase of loans for study.
- Parliament finally approved the auditors for the central bank after rural parties dropped their opposition.
- Central Tallinn district head Juri Ott wants to increase rents by ten times for cultural establishments.
- The U.S. Rand Corporation has predicted that the Baltic States will not be admitted to NATO in the first round.
- Police detained a businessman closely connected with the underground.
- The newspaper said that Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi wrongfully gained an appartment for his daughter in central Tallinn.
- Students in the key university town of Tartu plan more protests against cuts in public transport subsidies.
- The government plans to submit a draft law to parliament on the payment of bonds issued in 1927, now estimated to be worth 242 million kroons.
- A delegation from Korea's Daewoo corporation is to arrive for a visit to Estonia today to study investment opportunities.
